results.title: Will Ghana sustain policy reforms under IMF’s Poilcy Coordination Instrument? | CNBC Africa
results.snippet: Ghana’s first review under the International Monetary Fund’s Policy Coordination Instrument has entered its second week, with discussions focusing on the government’s ability to sustain policy reforms through revenue mobilisation, public debt management and the 2027 Budget. Richmond Frimpong, Co-Chair of the African SEZ Chamber, joins CNBC Africa for more on the outlook for Ghana’s reform agenda.
